summary: Dorian projects a holographic magnetosphere map across crustal sensors, assessing relativistic shear and grounding the kitchen spoons.
science_vegetable: Relativistic magnetohydrodynamic shear between the Red Giant's infrared coronal mass ejections and the Blue Dwarf's compressed ultraviolet bow shock.
text:
Dorian did not look at the world; he looked at the wireframe beneath it.

Standing before the Living Atlas, he adjusted the focal length of the crystalline projector. The holographic magnetosphere map hummed into existence, a sweeping three-dimensional web woven from the telemetry of thousands of crustal sensors. Bruised violet twilight cast double razor-sharp shadows across the hand-built brass observatory roof as the twin suns sank in discordant harmony. He watched the lines of force work to softly defend the structure, feeling the latent charge attract errant particles, threatening to consume the local power grid.

"The relativistic magnetohydrodynamic shear is spiking," Dorian muttered, tracing the violent intersection where the Red Giant's infrared coronal mass ejections collided with the Blue Dwarf's compressed ultraviolet bow shock. The friction between the two stellar behemoths was tearing the local flux lines to shreds.

He pulled his spectacles down, rubbing his temples as the weight of the data pressed against his rigid structural framework. The problem required a symphony of exactly fourteen variables to align perfectly, but the Enclave operated on stubborn, gritty pragmatism. He couldn't just model the abstract shear; he had to translate it into survival.

Leo ambled in, wiping grease from his hands with an oily rag. He squinted at the floating wireframe.

"Looks like a tangled spool of copper wire," Leo offered.

"If you're complaining and no one is laughing, you're complaining wrong," Dorian replied with dry, affectionate banter. "That 'spool' is a live projection of atmospheric ionization. The shear is turning the air conductive."

Under extreme stress, the measured archivist felt the sudden, hot surge of his Aries Vanguard override. He didn't just want to record the phenomenon; he wanted to force the Enclave to weather it through audacious action.

"Then today is a good day for science," Dorian declared, his voice ringing across the observatory. He slapped his hand on the console, collapsing the projection into localized sectors. "The ionization will seek the path of least resistance right into the Forge. Leo, you have to ground every metal soup spoon in the kitchen, or Ryn's stew is going to be served with a side of electrocution."

Leo stared at him, then let out a low chuckle. "Soup spoons. Right. I'll get the wire."

As Leo lumbered out, Jane slipped into the room, a data slate tucked under her arm. Dorian turned to her, gesturing at the still-humming projection. "The atmospheric variables are cascading, Jane. It's your turn to weave this chaos into a forecast."
